title: Spectral certificate value bound
statement:
Let $\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}}$, $N$, $D$, and $\norm{A}$ be real numbers with $D > 0$ and $N > 0$. If
\[
  \mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}} \;\le\; \frac{N}{D}\,\norm{A},
\]
then $\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}} \le \frac{N}{D}\,\norm{A}$.
caveat: The Lean statement is a tautology: its conclusion is verbatim its hypothesis, so the prose faithfully repeats the assumed inequality as the conclusion. The names $N$, $D$, $\norm{A}$ are plain real variables in the formal statement, carrying no built-in interpretation as binomial coefficients or a spectral norm, so no such interpretation is asserted here.
replaced:
For reals $\mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}}$, $N$, $D$ and $\norm{A}$ with $D > 0$ and $N > 0$,
if
\[
  \mathrm{val}_{f_{L,R}} \;\le\; \frac{N}{D}\,\norm{A},
\]
then the same bound holds. Here $N = \binom{2n}{\ell}$, $D = 2\binom{2n-4}{\ell-2}$,
and $\norm{A}$ is the spectral norm of the Kikuchi matrix $A$, so the statement records
the certificate $\mathrm{val}(f_{L,R}) \le (N/D)\,\norm{A}$.
